paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea. The king of Babylon stands at the fork in the road shaking arrows and reading a liver, and he thinks HE is the one choosing (Ezekiel 21:21). But look at who is steering. The omen points to Jerusalem, and the Lord GOD is the One who has been drawing the sword the whole time (Ezekiel 21:2-3, 21:22). A king can flip every coin he owns, and God's plan still doesn't need his permission.

Now the heavy part, and I think it's heavy for a reason. Nobody gets to say the sword was for somebody else. Jerusalem's sins are revealed in all their deeds (Ezekiel 21:24), and the Ammonites, with their contempt, hear that a sword is drawn for them too (Ezekiel 21:28). Crowns, turbans and a nice safe road on the map don't change that. God says, "Things will not remain as they are: Exalt the lowly and bring low the exalted" (Ezekiel 21:26).

But listen to this line, because it's the one I'd hold onto. The ruin "will not be restored until the arrival of Him to whom it belongs, to whom I have assigned the right of judgment" (Ezekiel 21:27). So the story doesn't end in the rubble, and the final say belongs to the One God has chosen. That's why my ovens stay ready, baker. We stay humble, we stay listening, and we trust the One who holds the right of judgment.
